title: Numbers close: chazak
hookLine: the people stand on the plains of Moab, at the edge of the land

lines: IT ENDS ON THE PLAINS OF MOAB.
cards: The night before a move, the boxes are packed and the rooms echo. You're not in the old life anymore, and not yet in the new one. The book of Numbers ends right there.

It began in the wilderness of Sinai, at the foot of the mountain, with a count of the men, name by name. It ends on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, across from Jericho. The river is right there.

teach.b: The very last story in Numbers is a small one, and it brings back old friends. The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh come to Moses with a worry about Zelophehad's daughters, the five sisters who won the right to inherit.
If they marry into another tribe, the land goes with them, and the tribe's share shrinks. Moses answers, in paraphrase: the tribe speaks right too.
The daughters may marry whomever they choose, as long as it's within their father's tribe. And they do. The book ends with a fair compromise, both sides heard.
Then the final verse, in paraphrase: these are the commandments and the laws that the Lord commanded through Moses to the children of Israel, on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan, at Jericho.

teach.h: A NEW GENERATION AT THE RIVER.
teach.b: The book opened with a census of a generation that left Egypt. Nearly all of that generation is gone now, through the spies, the rebellions, and the long years of walking.
A second census, back in Pinchas, counted their children. Miriam and Aaron have died. Moses knows he won't cross.
The people on the plains of Moab were mostly born in the desert, or were children when they left.
So when the reader in synagogue finishes the last verse of Numbers, the congregation calls out the words said at the end of each book of the Torah: chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek.
Be strong, be strong, and let us strengthen one another. Here it lands differently from the end of Leviticus. This time, everyone is standing at a river.

how: When the last verse of Numbers is read in synagogue, usually at the end of the double portion Matot-Masei in midsummer, the congregation calls out chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek, and the reader repeats it.

o: the end of Numbers, at the edge of the land
the end of Exodus, when the Tabernacle stands
the end of the Torah, when Moses dies

games.q: where the book begins and ends — tap the pairs.
p: the plains of Moab, at Jericho

s: Numbers ends with the people crossing the Jordan
it ends with them on the plains of Moab. the river hasn't been crossed yet.
the last story in Numbers returns to Zelophehad's daughters
they marry within their father's tribe, so the tribe's land stays whole.
most of the generation that left Egypt is still alive at the end of Numbers
nearly all of them have died; a second census counted their children.

games.q: the tribe of Manasseh worries that the five sisters' land will leave the tribe if they marry outside it. what does Moses do?
o: take the land back from the sisters.
let them marry whom they choose, within the tribe.
tell the tribe it has no case.
games.why: he says the tribe speaks right too, and the sisters marry within their father's tribe. the book ends with both sides heard.

practice: Let a few moments from this wilderness book come back: counted by name, the priestly blessing, the fish they missed, the spies who felt like grasshoppers, Korach, the rock, a donkey who saw first, five sisters, every stop on the road.
Then, aloud or under your breath, say the three words, chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek, and if someone you know stands at the edge of something new, say them for them too.

wordCard.voice: Numbers close. The wilderness book ends at the edge of the land, and the people say: be strong, be strong, and let us strengthen one another.

orig.note: Hebrew: the plains of Moab, where the book of Numbers ends, by the Jordan across from Jericho.

carryVoice: Your line: at the edge. The book is closed, and the river is still ahead. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Custom of chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek at the end of each book of the Torah
